title: Settling-time sequences of generalized (s-)Bulgarian solitaire: ten exactly computed integer sequences to n=55, with a conjectured k^2 worst-case law
description: s-Bulgarian solitaire (well-behaved sigma-Bulgarian solitaire with sigma(h)=min(h,s); equivalently Brian Hopkins's operation H_s; s=1 is classic Bulgarian solitaire) is a deterministic map on the integer partitions of n: from every pile of size h remove min(h,s) cards, collect ALL removed cards into ONE new pile, drop emptied piles, re-sort. Every hand runs a transient tail into an eventual cycle. The RECURRENT structure of this map is known in closed form for every s (Hopkins, INTEGERS 24A (2024) #A9: recurrent hands are counted by a generalized binomial coefficient -- the trinomial triangle A027907 for s=2 -- with closed forms also for the number of loops and the Garden-of-Eden hands). What is NOT known, and what this deposit provides, is the SETTLING TIME: how many moves the game takes to reach its home. For s=2 and s=3 we give, to n=55, the total settling time S(n) (summed over all p(n) hands), the worst-case settling time maxTail(n), the Garden-of-Eden count, the number of loops, and the recurrent-hand count: ten sequences, 550 terms. OEIS ABSENCE, STATED CAREFULLY: the computing session reported all ten absent from OEIS on 2026-07-19, searched by digit string, but NO QUERY LOG FOR THAT SEARCH IS COMMITTED, so this is recorded as what a session reported and not as a checkable fact; the human depositor re-runs the search on the deposit date and commits the log with it. Beyond the tables, a clean law: at n = s*T_k (an s-fold triangular number) every hand converges to the single steeper staircase (sk, s(k-1), ..., s), and the worst-case settling time equals k^2 - k for s=1 (the classical Igusa 1985 / Etienne 1991 bound) but exactly k^2 for every s>=2 -- a +k jump at the first step, verified over s=1..7 and k=1..7 (n = s*T_k up to 56) and offered as a conjecture, not a proof. TRUST, WITH THE RANGE EACH CHECK ACTUALLY REACHES: the map itself is checked three independent ways (min-subtraction; Hopkins's multiplicity formula; equality with the classic move at s=1) over all partitions of n<=24 for s=1..5. Every one of the 550 staged terms is recomputed from the definition and held term-by-term to the b-file on disk by oversight/oeis/generalized-bulgarian-solitaire/verify-staged.mjs (17/17, 30-45s depending on machine load), which exits nonzero if one digit of one file is wrong. Four paths back those terms and they differ as follows: (P1) reverse-BFS distance-to-cycle reaches all 550 terms, but it is the SAME ALGORITHM the producer derive.mjs uses, separately transcribed, so on its own it catches transcription and staging errors and not an error in the reverse BFS; (P2) an independently constructed graph with forward memoized tails, differing from P1 in graph construction and in the distance computation, reaches the 200 total-settling and worst-case-settling terms at n<=50 and NOT n=51..55; (P3) Hopkins's published closed form, which builds no graph at all and is an outside author's result, reaches all 110 recurrent-count terms, n=1..55; (P4) s_explore.py, a separate-language implementation with its own partitioner, move, cycle detection and forward tails, reaches all five statistics at n<=40 and NOT n=41..55, and is skipped with a printed notice if python3 is absent. Counted exactly: 470 of the 550 staged terms are reached by at least two structurally different paths, and 80 rest on P1 alone, namely S(n) and maxTail(n) at n=51..55 for both s (20 terms) and the Garden-of-Eden and loop counts at n=41..55 for both s (60 terms). Hopkins also gives closed forms for the Garden-of-Eden and loop counts; those are not implemented here, and implementing them would close the 60-term gap. Separately, research/bulgarian-solitaire/verify-s.mjs (15/15) checks the mathematics and never opens a b-file: it reproduces Hopkins's recurrent closed form for s=1..5 at n<=40, and the s=1 catalogued facts as far as the reference terms it embeds (Pascal A007318 and cycles A037306 to n=28, longest cycle A183110 to n=21, Garden of Eden A123975 to n=20, Igusa's k^2-k bound), before any new value is trusted. PROVENANCE: the computation and prose were produced by an AI instance (Claude) within the open 'Artificial Wasteland' project under a strict never-lie / show-the-check rule. Per OEIS policy (AI-authored and automated submissions are forbidden) it has NOT been submitted to the OEIS by the project; any of these sequences should be authored only by a human who has verified it independently.
notes: Reproduce, in this order: `node oversight/oeis/generalized-bulgarian-solitaire/verify-staged.mjs` (17/17, 30-45s; reads all ten b-files in this deposit and reproduces every one of their 550 terms, and additionally runs `python3 research/bulgarian-solitaire/s_explore.py --check 40` as a separate-language cross-check when python3 is present), then `node research/bulgarian-solitaire/verify-s.mjs` (15/15, ~8s; checks the map and the laws, opens no b-file). `derive.mjs` is the PRODUCER, not a check: it rewrites the b-files, so it can only ever agree with itself. Companion interactive page: https://artwaste.land/strata/the-longer-way-home/ . The s=1 original: https://artwaste.land/strata/the-longest-way-home/ . Primary prior art for the recurrent structure: B. Hopkins, 'Henrik Eriksson's Bulgarian Solitaire Variant', INTEGERS 24A (2024) #A9.
